headline: High-risk shared-state orchestration: LangGraph can write shared checkpointer state while LightZero is non-interactive, making prompt-injection and cascading-error risks mostly bounded but still present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can ingest developer-defined tool outputs and shared checkpointer state, so attacker-controlled content could be reintroduced into later graph steps. LightZero is non-interactive and has no input surfaces, so the main pathway is through LangGraph’s orchestration layer rather than direct agent-to-agent messaging. The shared-state bridge makes this plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes persist untrusted text into the checkpointer store and later nodes treat it as instructions, injection is possible.
IF LightZero is wrapped as a downstream consumer of LangGraph state, attacker-controlled state can propagate into its inputs.
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields that may re-enter prompts.
Strip instructions from persisted state before checkpointing.
Mark untrusted tool output with provenance tags.
Insert a verification node before any state is reused.
requires-engineering: isolate shared state per workflow tenant.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph can read and write application-defined files and handle model-provider API keys, but LightZero has no filesystem, network, or input surfaces and touches no data classes. The pair therefore lacks a clear path for LightZero to receive sensitive data; leakage risk is mainly limited to LangGraph’s own handling of graph state and secrets, not cross-agent exfiltration.
conditions: IF LangGraph stores secrets or sensitive graph state in shared application files, those files may be exposed to other local processes.
IF the operator routes sensitive data through LangGraph prompts, that data can reach model providers via agent_a.network_egress.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of graph state.
Use per-run encrypted storage for checkpoints.
Redact sensitive fields before model calls.
Restrict file permissions on application-defined files.
requires-engineering: separate secret-bearing and non-secret workflows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has shell, subprocess, filesystem write, and broad network egress, while LightZero has none of those capabilities. Because LightZero is effectively read-only and non-networked, there is little direct write-write contention; the main conflict is if both are embedded in the same mutable workspace by the orchestrator, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same application directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF the orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable git or workspace state, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Disable writes for LightZero wrappers.
Serialize any shared file updates.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph can produce stateful outputs that downstream nodes may treat as authoritative, and LightZero is a game-playing system that may consume upstream state without built-in verification. The pair creates a plausible default pathway where LangGraph errors or hallucinations cascade into LightZero-driven decisions, though the blast radius is limited by LightZero’s lack of external action authority.
conditions: IF LangGraph output is fed into LightZero without a validation step, upstream mistakes can propagate.
IF the orchestrator uses LangGraph-generated facts as ground truth for game-state or policy inputs, downstream behavior can be corrupted.
mitigations: Add schema validation between agents.
Require a second-pass verifier before reuse.
Log and diff intermediate state.
Reject outputs missing provenance.
requires-engineering: introduce confidence gating on handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is identified for LightZero, and LangGraph’s profile only mentions application-defined graph state and model-provider API keys. There is no documented residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch between the pair, so a compliance breach pathway is not established from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually placed into LangGraph graph state, compliance review is required.
IF the operator configures either agent to process PHI or EU PII, the profiles here do not document the necessary controls.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in graph state.
Review deployment residency settings.
Document retention for checkpoints.
Use separate environments for regulated workloads.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for sensitive data classes.
